name: Geelong CBD and Waterfront
tagline: The bay frontage, the bollards and the station
description: The centre between Malop Street and Corio Bay, redeveloped around the waterfront promenade with its carousel, swimming enclosure and the painted bollards that have become the city's emblem. The station, the coworking and most of the apartments are here, and Melbourne is an hour by train.
bestFor: Working without a car, with the train to Melbourne on hand
pros: Train to Melbourne from the centre
Most apartments and coworking in the city
cons: Quiet in the evening once offices empty
Corio Bay is calm rather than surf
Some streets feel bleak in winter

name: Newtown
tagline: Heritage streets and the Pakington Street strip
description: The oldest residential suburb, west of the centre, with bluestone and weatherboard houses on wide streets and Pakington Street running through it as Geelong's best eating and shopping strip. It is the most attractive part of the city to live in and the rents reflect that.
bestFor: Longer stays where character and cafes matter
pros: Pakington Street's cafes, bars and shops
Ten minutes on foot to the centre
cons: The most expensive rentals in Geelong
Parking on Pakington is a daily annoyance

name: Belmont
tagline: South of the river, cheaper and family-shaped
description: A large residential suburb across the Barwon River from the centre, built around High Street's shops and the river parklands. Rents drop noticeably here and the Barwon River trail runs along the northern edge, which is the best flat cycling and running in the city.
bestFor: Budget-conscious stays with space and a river path
pros: Cheaper than anything north of the river
Barwon River trail for running and cycling
cons: Traffic across the river bridges at peak

name: Waurn Ponds
tagline: The Deakin campus edge, newer and further out
description: The southwestern fringe around Deakin University's main Geelong campus and the shopping centre beside it, with newer housing estates and a train station on the Warrnambool line. It is where much of the city's student and research population lives and the ring road is close.
bestFor: Anyone with university business or wanting newer housing
pros: Newer housing stock with better insulation
Train station and ring road access
Closest to the Great Ocean Road turnoff
cons: Fifteen minutes from the centre by car

name: Barwon Heads and Ocean Grove
tagline: Surf coast villages twenty-five minutes south
description: Two adjoining coastal towns at the mouth of the Barwon, with a proper ocean beach, a bluff walk and a village centre that fills every summer with Melbourne families. It is a different life from the city, and many people who work in Geelong choose to live here instead.
bestFor: Anyone prioritising ocean beach over city convenience
pros: Bellarine rail trail and wineries nearby
cons: Twenty-five minutes from Geelong by car
Prices spike over the summer holidays
